title: Image provenance tagging + delta-SBOM generator for driver-compatible upgrades
creator: Priya Nair
description:
Problem: Upgrades to runtime images sometimes regressed GPU-driver compatibility or introduced supply-chain changes that were hard to audit during canary rollouts. We need an automated way to publish precise provenance, produce delta SBOMs for image upgrades, and validate CUDA/driver compatibility in the upgrade pipeline prior to canary promotion.

Goals:
- Define a readable, machine-friendly image provenance tag schema that encodes runtime semantic version, immutable digest, and driver profile (e.g. redwood/runtime:1.20.3+sha256-<digest>-cuda12.1-driver535).
- Generate delta SBOMs for any image diff between two releases (base -> candidate) and surface added/removed packages and layers in the pipeline UI.
- Implement an automated driver-compatibility validator using our driver matrix to fail upgrades when the candidate image requires drivers outside pinned LTS ranges for a given dedicated pool.
- Integrate gating: pipeline will block canary promotion if delta-SBOM shows new high-risk packages (based on vulnerability score threshold) or if driver-compat check fails.

Scope and deliverables:
1) Tagging: schema + tooling to re-tag images on push. Backwards compatible: accept existing tags but add new provenance tags for upcoming releases.
2) Delta SBOM generator: GitHub Action that extracts SBOMs from container layers (syft), computes delta, and persists both full and delta SBOM to object storage.
3) Driver-compat validator: microservice that consults the canonical driver matrix (stored in repo) and returns a pass/fail plus recommended fallback image variant.
4) Pipeline integration: add checks to release GH Actions and Dedicated/Private upgrade pipeline; expose results to Console rollout gates (block-if-fail).
5) Docs + runbook + test plan.

Acceptance criteria:
- New provenance tag format published in docs and used for all runtime-1.20 candidate images.
- Delta SBOM produced for a sample image pair (<2 minutes for typical 1.2GB image) and stored at s3://redwood-release-sboms/<release>/delta.json.
- Driver-compat validator correctly flags three simulated mismatches in unit tests and returns recommended alternate image variant when available.
- Console rollout gate blocks canary promotion when validator fails in an end-to-end dry run.

Non-goals:
- Rewriting existing SBOM pipeline for all teams (we will add compatibility adapters).
- Automatic driver upgrades on customer hardware (we only block/advise).

Design notes and trade-offs:
- Delta SBOMs reduce storage and review burden vs storing full SBOMs for every image, but add complexity to generation logic. We'll store both full and delta for auditability.
- Tag schema balances human-readability and strict immutability: we keep digest-based primary identity but add a suffix with driver profile. This avoids accidental redeploy by tag.
- We will prefer syft for SBOM extraction for speed and widespread OSS tooling, but keep an adapter interface in case we swap to in-house tooling later.

Success metrics:
- 100% of runtime candidate builds have provenance tags in the release-1.20 cycle.
- Reduction of post-rollout driver-related incidents by 90% for runtime-1.20 rollouts.
- Time to produce delta SBOM <= 2 minutes in 95th percentile for typical images.

Risks:
- False positives in driver-compat validator causing unnecessary blockages. Mitigation: staged rollout with canary-only advisory mode for two cycles before enforcing hard blocks.
- Increased CI time for release jobs. Mitigation: cache layer digests and run delta-SBOM only when base digest differs.
